action.action-desc: Mr. Wyden (for himself and Mr. Merkley) introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources

form.official-title: To provide for the establishment of a grazing management program on Federal land in Malheur County, Oregon, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Malheur Community Empowerment for the Owyhee Act.

paragraph.text: The term Bureau means the Bureau of Land Management.
The term Commissioner means the Commissioner of Reclamation.
The term County means Malheur County, Oregon.
The term Federal land means land in the County managed by the Bureau.

The term long-term ecological health, with respect to an ecosystem, means the ability of the ecological processes of the ecosystem to function in a manner that maintains the composition, structure, activity, and resilience of the ecosystem over time, including an ecologically appropriate diversity of plant and animal communities, habitats, and conditions that are sustainable through successional processes.

subparagraph.text: The term loop road means a route managed and maintained by the Bureau or the County, as applicable, for the purpose of providing directed tourism and educational opportunities in the County.
The term loop road includes each of the roads described in paragraphs (2) through (5) of section 6(b).

paragraph.text: The term Malheur CEO Group means the Malheur Community Empowerment for Owyhee Group established under section 4(a).

The term operational flexibility, with respect to grazing on the Federal land, means any approved seasonal adjustments of livestock positioning for the purposes of that grazing pursuant to a flexible grazing use authorized under the program.
The term program means the Malheur County Grazing Management Program authorized under section 3(a).
The term Secretary means the Secretary of the Interior.
The term State means the State of Oregon.

subsection.text: The Secretary may carry out a grazing management program on the Federal land, to be known as the Malheur County Grazing Management Program, in accordance with the memorandum entitled Bureau of Land Management Instruction Memorandum 2018–109, to provide to authorized grazing permittees and lessees increased operational flexibility to improve the long-term ecological health of the Federal land.

paragraph.header: Flexible grazing use alternative for a grazing permit or lease
paragraph.text: For purposes of renewing a grazing permit or lease under the program, pursuant to the National Environmental Policy Act of 1969 (42 U.S.C. 4321 et seq.), the Secretary shall develop and analyze at least 1 alternative to provide operational flexibility in livestock grazing use to account for changing conditions.

paragraph.header: Interim flexible grazing use for a grazing permit or lease
paragraph.text: For purposes of using operational flexibility pending the renewal of a grazing permit or lease under the program, the Bureau may authorize temporary changes in livestock grazing use in accordance with applicable laws (including regulations) after providing notice to the applicable individuals and entities described in paragraph (3).
The Secretary shall develop alternatives under paragraph (1) in consultation with—

subparagraph.text: the applicable grazing permittee or lessee;
affected Federal and State agencies;
the Malheur CEO Group;
other landowners in the affected allotment; and
interested members of the public.

The Secretary shall develop cooperative rangeland monitoring plans and rangeland health objectives to apply to actions taken under paragraph (1) or (2) and to improve the long-term ecological health of the Federal land under the program, in consultation with grazing permittees or lessees and other individuals and entities described in paragraph (3).
A monitoring plan developed under subparagraph (A) shall—

clause.text: identify situations in which providing operational flexibility in grazing permit or lease uses is appropriate to improve long-term ecological health of the Federal land;
identify ways in which progress would be measured toward long-term ecological health of the Federal land;
include—

subclause.text: a description of the condition standards for which the monitoring is tracking, including baseline conditions and desired outcome conditions;
a description of monitoring methods and protocols;
an identification of the responsible party for data collection and storage;
a description of the anticipated use of the data;
provisions for adjusting any components of the monitoring plan; and
a description of the method to communicate the criteria for adjusting livestock grazing use; and

clause.text: provide for annual reports on the effects of operational flexibility in grazing permit or lease uses under the program.

subparagraph.text: If the Secretary determines that an alternative considered under the program that provides operational flexibility is the preferred alternative, the Secretary shall incorporate the alternative, including applicable monitoring plans developed under paragraph (4), into the terms and conditions of the applicable grazing permit or lease.

Before implementing any measure for purposes of operational flexibility with respect to a grazing use authorized under the terms and conditions of a permit or lease with respect to which an alternative has been incorporated under subparagraph (A), the grazing permittee or lessee shall notify the Secretary in writing of the proposed adjustment.
The Secretary may include any other requirements in a permit or lease with respect to which an alternative has been incorporated under subparagraph (A) that the Secretary determines to be necessary.

Subject to subparagraph (B), not earlier than the date that is 8 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall conduct a review of the program to determine whether the objectives of the program are being met.

subparagraph.header: No effect on program permits and leases
subparagraph.text: The review of the program under subparagraph (A) shall not affect the existence, renewal, or termination of a grazing permit or lease entered into under the program.

paragraph.text: If, based on the review conducted under paragraph (1), the Secretary determines that the objectives of the program are not being met, the Secretary shall, on the date that is 10 years after the date of enactment of this Act—

subparagraph.text: modify the program in a manner to ensure that the objectives of the program would be met; or
terminate the program.

subsection.header: No effect on grazing rights or privileges

paragraph.text: affects the rights or privileges provided under the Act of 10 June 28, 1934 (commonly known as the Taylor Grazing Act; 43 U.S.C. 315 et seq.); or
requires the Secretary to consider modifying or terminating the classification of any existing grazing district on the Federal land in any subsequent plan or decision of the Secretary.

section.header: Malheur Community Empowerment for Owyhee Group

subsection.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall establish an advisory group, to be known as the Malheur Community Empowerment for Owyhee Group—

paragraph.text: to provide to the Secretary advice and recommendations relating to the implementation of actions proposed to be carried out under this Act, including monitoring and operational flexibility of grazing use of the Federal land;
to be listed as an interested party for pending Bureau management decisions on the Federal land under this Act; and
to provide advice and recommendations to the State and the County commissioners on economic development issues relating to the Federal land under this Act.
The Malheur CEO Group shall consist of—

subparagraph.text: 8 voting members, to be appointed by the Secretary, based on recommendations from the Vale District Bureau manager and the County commissioners, of whom—

clause.text: 3 shall be representatives of grazing permittees and lessees in the County;
3 shall be representatives of other businesses or conservation or recreation organizations in the County, of whom at least 2 shall reside in the County;
1 shall be a representative of the Burns Paiute Tribe; and
1 shall be a representative of the Fort McDermott Tribe; and

subparagraph.text: 4 nonvoting members, to be appointed by the Secretary, based on recommendations from the Vale District Bureau manager and the County commissioners, of whom—

clause.text: 1 shall be a representative of the Bureau Vale District;
1 shall be a representative of the United States Fish and Wildlife Service;
1 shall be a representative of the State; and
1 shall be a representative of the County.

subparagraph.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall appoint the initial members of the Malheur CEO Group.
Each member of the Malheur CEO Group shall serve for a term of 3 years.
A member of the Malheur CEO Group may be reappointed for 1 or more additional 3-year terms.
A vacancy on the Malheur CEO Group shall be filled—

clause.text: as soon as practicable after the vacancy occurs; and
in the same manner as the original appointment.

subparagraph.text: Members of the Malheur CEO Group shall serve without compensation.

Each member of the Malheur CEO Group shall receive from the Secretary travel expenses, including per diem in lieu of subsistence, in accordance with sections 5702 and 5703 of title 5, United States Code.

paragraph.text: A chairperson shall be elected by a majority of the voting members of the Malheur CEO Group.
The representative from the Bureau Vale District appointed under paragraph (1)(B)(i) shall be—

subparagraph.text: the secretary and recordkeeper for the Malheur CEO Group; and
responsible for convening meetings of the Malheur CEO Group.

paragraph.text: The Malheur CEO Group shall—

subparagraph.text: review any program project proposed to the Bureau by—

clause.text: a member of the Malheur CEO Group;
a grazing permittee or lessee on the Federal land; or
any other member of the public;

subparagraph.text: subject to paragraph (2), propose program projects and funding recommendations to the Secretary under this section;
cooperate with appropriate officials of land management agencies in the County in recommending program projects consistent with purposes of this section;
review program monitoring data and, in accordance with this subsection, recommend program project modifications, if appropriate; and

provide frequent opportunities for citizens, organizations, Indian Tribes, land management agencies, and other interested parties to participate openly and meaningfully in program project development and implementation.

paragraph.text: The Malheur CEO Group may propose a program project to the Secretary if the program project has been approved by a majority of the members voting at an official meeting of the Malheur CEO Group.
A quorum is required for an official meeting of the Malheur CEO Group.
The Malheur CEO Group shall hold official meetings not less frequently than biannually.
An official meeting of the Malheur CEO Group may be held virtually.
A quorum of the Malheur CEO Group shall consist of a majority of the members of the Malheur CEO Group participating in person or virtually.
Each meeting of the Malheur CEO Group shall—

subparagraph.text: not later than the date that is 1 week before the date of the meeting, be announced—

clause.text: on the public website of the Bureau; and
in a local newspaper of record, as determined by the Secretary; and

subparagraph.text: be held open to the public.

paragraph.text: The secretary of the Malheur CEO Group described in subsection (b)(5) shall—

subparagraph.text: maintain records of each official meeting of the Malheur CEO Group; and
make the records maintained under subparagraph (A) available for public inspection.

paragraph.text: The members of the Malheur CEO Group shall establish bylaws for the Malheur CEO Group.
Bylaws may be established under paragraph (1) on approval by a majority of the members of the Malheur CEO Group.

subsection.text: During any period in which the program and the Malheur CEO Group are in existence, the Secretary shall consult with the Malheur CEO Group—

paragraph.text: not less frequently than once every 60 days; or
as otherwise agreed to by—

subparagraph.text: the Secretary; and
the Malheur CEO Group.

subsection.text: The Federal Advisory Committee Act (5 U.S.C. App.) shall not apply to the Malheur CEO Group.

paragraph.text: There is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out this section $51,000 for each of fiscal years 2023 through 2027.
Of the amounts made available under paragraph (1), not more than 10 percent may be used for administrative costs relating to the Malheur CEO Group.

The term wilderness area means a wilderness area designated by subsection (b)(1).

As soon as practicable after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall prepare and submit to Congress a map and legal description of each wilderness area.

Each map and legal description prepared under subparagraph (A) shall have the same force and effect as if included in this Act, except that the Secretary may correct clerical and typographical errors in the map or legal description.
The maps and legal descriptions prepared under subparagraph (A) shall be on file and available for public inspection in the appropriate offices of the Bureau.
Subject to valid existing rights, the wilderness areas shall be administered by the Secretary in accordance with the Wilderness Act (16 U.S.C. 1131 et seq.), except that—

clause.text: any reference in that Act to the effective date of that Act shall be considered to be a reference to the date of enactment of this Act; and
any reference in that Act to the Secretary of Agriculture shall be considered to be a reference to the Secretary.

subparagraph.text: The Secretary shall allow the continuation of the grazing of livestock, including the maintenance, construction, or replacement of authorized supporting facilities, in the wilderness areas, if established before the date of enactment of this Act, in accordance with—

clause.text: section 4(d)(4) of the Wilderness Act (16 U.S.C. 1133(d)(4)); and
the guidelines set forth in Appendix A of the report of the Committee on Interior and Insular Affairs of the House of Representatives accompanying H.R. 2570 of the 101st Congress (H. Rept. 101–405).

subparagraph.text: The Secretary may carry out any activities in the wilderness areas that the Secretary determines to be necessary for the control of fire, insects, and diseases, in accordance with—

clause.text: section 4(d)(1) of the Wilderness Act (16 U.S.C. 1133(d)(1)); and
the report of the Committee on Interior and Insular Affairs of the House of Representatives accompanying H.R. 1437 of the 98th Congress (House Report 98–40).

subparagraph.text: Nothing in this Act requires the closure of any adjacent road outside the boundary of a wilderness area.

subsection.header: Management of land not designated as wilderness

subparagraph.text: Congress finds that, for purposes of section 603(c) of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 (43 U.S.C. 1782(c)), any portion of the Federal land designated as a wilderness study area, as depicted on the Map, on the date of enactment of this Act that is not designated as wilderness by subsection (b)(1) has been adequately studied for wilderness designation.
Except as provided in paragraph (2), the land described in subparagraph (A)—

clause.text: is no longer subject to section 603(c) of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 (43 U.S.C. 1782(c)); and

shall be managed in accordance with the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 (43 U.S.C. 1701 et seq.), including any applicable land use plan adopted under section 202 of that Act (43 U.S.C. 1712).

paragraph.header: Management of certain land with wilderness characteristics
paragraph.text: Any portion of the Federal land that was previously determined by the Secretary to be land with wilderness characteristics that is not designated as wilderness by subsection (b)(1) shall be managed by the Secretary in accordance with the applicable land use plans adopted under section 202 of the Federal Land Policy and Management Act of 1976 (43 U.S.C. 1712).

subsection.text: In this section, the term Map means the map entitled Lake Owyhee, Succor Creek, Birch Creek, and Three Forks Scenic Loops and dated November 6, 2019.

paragraph.text: The Secretary, in coordination with the County, shall work with Travel Oregon to establish the loop roads.

clause.text: The Secretary shall seek to enter into an arrangement with the County to fund safety upgrades, in accordance with County road standards, to the Owyhee Dam Road to ensure access to the recreational opportunities of the Owyhee Reservoir, including improved signage and surfacing.
Any upgrades carried out with funds provided under clause (i) shall be completed not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, weather permitting.

If the County receives any funds under this subparagraph, the County shall ensure that, not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, weather permitting, the Owyhee Dam Road is in compliance with the applicable standards of—

subparagraph.text: In addition to amounts made available under subsection (f)(1), there is authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary to carry out subparagraph (A) $6,000,000.

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall work with the County on a plan to improve the Succor Creek Scenic Loop, as generally depicted on the Map, to accommodate visitors and residents.
The Secretary shall work with the County on a plan to improve the Birch Creek Scenic Loop, as generally depicted on the Map, to accommodate visitors and residents.
The Secretary shall work with the County on a plan to improve the Three Forks Scenic Loop, as generally depicted on the Map—

subparagraph.text: to accommodate visitors and residents; and
to provide a connection to the Idaho Scenic Byway.

subsection.header: Improvements to state parks and other amenities
subsection.text: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act—

paragraph.text: the Commissioner, in coordination with the Owyhee Irrigation District, shall work with Travel Oregon or the Oregon Parks and Recreation Department, as appropriate, to carry out a feasibility study regarding each of—

subparagraph.text: the establishment of not more than 2 marinas on the Owyhee Reservoir;
improvements to existing Oregon State Parks bordering the Owyhee Reservoir;
the establishment of a network of hostelries in the County using former hotels and bunkhouses that are not currently in use;
improvements to private camps on the shore of the Owyhee Reservoir;
the establishment of a dude ranch at Birch Creek; and
any other economic development proposals for the Owyhee Reservoir or the County; and

paragraph.text: the Secretary shall work with the County to carry out a feasibility study regarding the rails-to-trails project known as Rails to Trails: The Oregon Eastern Branch/The Oregon and Northwestern Railroad.

subsection.text: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary, in coordination with Travel Oregon, shall complete a feasibility study on how best to market communities or sections of the County as the Gateway to the Oregon Owyhee.

subsection.header: Jordan valley airstrip improvements To support firefighting efforts

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall work with firefighting entities in the County to determine—

subparagraph.text: the need for the use of the Jordan Valley Airstrip to support firefighting efforts; and
the conditions under which the Jordan Valley Airstrip may be used to support firefighting efforts.

paragraph.text: Not later than 1 year after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall submit to the Malheur CEO Group a report describing the need and conditions described in subparagraphs (A) and (B) of paragraph (1), including methods by which to meet those conditions.

subsection.text: There are authorized to be appropriated for fiscal year 2023—

paragraph.text: to the Secretary—

subparagraph.text: to carry out subsection (b), $2,000,000;
to carry out subsection (c)(2), $2,000,000;
to carry out subsection (d), $500,000; and
to carry out subsection (e), $500,000; and

paragraph.text: to the Commissioner to carry out subsection (c)(1), $1,000,000.

section.header: Land conveyance to Burns Paiute Tribe

subsection.text: As soon as practicable after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall—

paragraph.text: transfer to the Burns Paiute Tribe all right, title, and interest in and to the land in the State described in subsection (b) for the purpose of protecting and conserving cultural and natural values and to be part of the reservation of the Burns Paiute Tribe; and
take the land transferred under paragraph (1) into trust for the benefit of the Burns Paiute Tribe.

subsection.text: The land referred to in subsection (a)(1) is the following, as depicted on the map entitled Malheur Reservation Paiute Indian Tribe Grant, Malheur, and Harney Counties, Oregon and dated March 15, 1958:

paragraph.text: The parcel commonly known as Jonesboro Ranch, located approximately 6 miles east of Juntura, Oregon, consisting of 21,548 acres of Federal land, 6,686 acres of certain private land associated with the Jonesboro Ranch containing the pastures referred to as Saddle Horse and Trail Horse, Indian Creek, Sperry Creek, Antelope Swales, Horse Camp, Dinner Creek, Upper Hunter Creek, and Tim’s Peak, and more particularly described as follows:

subparagraph.text: T. 20 S., R. 38 E., secs. 25 and 36.

paragraph.text: The approximately 4,137 acres of State land containing the pastures referred to as “Road Gulch” and “Black Canyon” and more particularly described as follows:

subsection.text: Land taken into trust under subsection (a)(2) shall be administered in accordance with the laws (including regulations) generally applicable to property held in trust by the United States for the benefit of an Indian Tribe.
As soon as practicable after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall prepare a map depicting the land taken into trust under subsection (a)(2).

Not later than 3 years after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall seek to enter into an agreement with the State under which the Secretary would exchange Federal land for the portions of the area described in subsection (b)(2) that are owned by the State.

subsection.header: Payment in lieu of taxes program
subsection.text: Any land taken into trust under subsection (a)(2) shall be eligible for payments under the payment in lieu of taxes program established under chapter 69 of title 31, United States Code.
There are authorized to be appropriated to the Secretary such sums as are necessary to carry out this section.

section.header: Effect on Tribal rights and certain existing uses
section.text: Nothing in this Act, including any designation or nondesignation of land transferred into trust to be held by the United States for the benefit of the Burns Paiute Tribe under section 7—

paragraph.text: alters, modifies, enlarges, diminishes, or abrogates rights secured by a treaty, statute, Executive order, or other Federal law of any Indian Tribe, including off-reservation reserved rights; or
affects—

subparagraph.text: existing rights-of-way; or
preexisting grazing uses and existing water rights or mining claims, except as specifically negotiated between any applicable Indian Tribe and the Secretary.
